newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-MCGEECHAN OUT OF RUNNING FOR ENGLAND JOB.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MCGEECHAN OUT OF RUNNING FOR ENGLAND JOB.

text.p: Victorious British Lions coach Ian McGeechan has ruled himself out of consideration for the job of England coach and will stay at Northampton.

English rugby head Fran Cotton, who worked closely with McGeechan on the Lions tour, said last week that he thought the former Scottish international centre was the best man for the post, currently filled part-time by Jack Rowell.
Rowell's contract expires at the end of August and Cotton has made it clear that he wants a full time appointment. Rowell is reluctant to give up his business interests to go full time.
But McGeechan, who coached Scotland to the Grand Slam in 1990 and the Lions on three tours culminating in this year's series win in South Africa, announced on Monday that he was to stay at his club.
In discussions with the RFU, Northampton reportedly demanded huge financial compensation to break McGeechan's contract which still has six years to run.
